finding.claim: [medium] exp=0 in the payload is silently dropped, so the signer mints a token with no exp that never expires.
finding.source: Caller-supplied payload.exp equal to 0 (for example a timestamp computed as 0 or defaulted to 0 from request data). Precondition: no expiresIn option.
finding.sink: Token issuance: a signed JWT with no exp claim, which the verifier then accepts indefinitely.

trace.note: Validation 'if (payload.exp && ...)' is falsy for 0, so the integer check is skipped.
exp ternary: 'payload.exp ? payload.exp : undefined' treats 0 as absent, so exp becomes undefined.
JSON.stringify omits undefined fields, so exp is absent from the encoded payload.
'if (!(claim in payload)) continue' skips the exp validator (verifier.js:606-614) when exp is absent.

finding.guards_checked: signer.js:75 integer check (bypassed for 0); signer.js:100 truthiness (drops 0); verifier.js:293-299 requiredClaims (opt-in only, not on by default). Repro: createSigner({key:'secret',algorithm:'HS256'})({sub:'a',exp:0}) then createVerifier({key:'secret',algorithms:['HS256']})(token) should succeed.

finding.claim: [medium-low] Token strings are not canonical. Base64url trailing pad bits and ECDSA high-S (or PSS randomness) give many valid string forms of one token, so any raw-token-string denylist or one-time-use check can be bypassed.
finding.source: Any previously issued valid token (the holder, or an attacker who observed it).
finding.sink: Protected operation: revocation or replay checks keyed on the raw token string; the signature is still accepted.

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE checks the charset only, not canonical encoding.
Signature segment passes the charset check.
Buffer.from(signature,'base64') ignores the unused low bits of the last char, so a variant decodes to identical bytes.
HMAC/RSA compare sees identical bytes, so verification passes for the variant string.
ES path: joseToDer does no low-S normalization, so (r, n-s) also verifies; PS256 signatures are randomized.

finding.guards_checked: decoder.js:35-43 charset regex; verifier.js:169 signature check. No canonical-length or trailing-bit check, and no low-S check. Repro: flip the low 2 bits of the last signature char of a valid HS256 token; it should still verify.

finding.claim: [low] With cache enabled, a Buffer token makes verify() throw a raw TypeError instead of a TokenError.
finding.source: Caller passes a Buffer token (advertised as supported at verifier.js:353 and decoder.js:14) to a verifier created with cache: true.
finding.sink: Error path: a non-TokenError escapes verify(), breaking error mapping (likely 500 instead of 401) and crashing callback-style callers.

trace.note: Buffer tokens pass the type check.
Cache lookup calls cacheKeyBuilder(token) before any decode.
Default cacheKeyBuilder is hashToken.
token.split('.', 1) is not a function on a Buffer, so TypeError is thrown.

finding.guards_checked: verifier.js:353 type check accepts Buffer; cache is opt-in (createCache at verifier.js:83-85 returns null by default). Repro: createVerifier({key,algorithms:['HS256'],cache:true})(Buffer.from(token)).

finding.claim: [low] maxAge is silently not enforced for tokens with no iat claim, so such tokens never age out by maxAge.
finding.source: A token signed without iat (signer noTimestamp:true, or any issuer omitting iat). The attacker needs a token from the issuer, so this is a configuration/issuer-behavior precondition.

trace.note: noTimestamp sets iat to undefined, so iat is absent.
claim not in payload: validator skipped.
maxAge validator is only added as a check on iat; nothing requires iat when maxAge is set.

finding.guards_checked: verifier.js:293-299 requiredClaims (opt-in); no check that iat exists when maxAge is configured. Repro: signer with noTimestamp:true, verifier with maxAge:60000, token still accepted later.

finding.claim: [low] crit header is skipped when falsy (false, 0, '', null), contrary to RFC 7515 4.1.11, so unknown critical markers are not rejected.
finding.source: A signed token whose header has crit set to a falsy non-array value (issuer-generated; the header is covered by the signature).
finding.sink: Protected operation: rejection of tokens carrying critical extensions the verifier does not understand.

trace.note: 'if (!header.crit) return' exits before the array and non-empty checks.
'ext in header' uses the prototype chain, so inherited names (e.g. constructor) pass the presence check if allowed.

finding.guards_checked: verifier.js:226-261 checks run only for truthy crit; allowedCritHeaders Set (verifier.js:578). Repro: header {alg:'HS256',crit:false} signed with the shared secret is accepted.

finding.claim: [low, config-dependent] In sync mode, a PEM public key with HS-only algorithms is used as an HMAC secret with no key-type check; the async path rejects the same config. Anyone holding the public PEM can mint accepted HS256 tokens.
finding.source: Operator configures algorithms ['HS256'] with a public-key PEM (the PEM is public). Attacker has the public PEM and signs HS256 tokens.

trace.note: Key is a string, so detection runs.
allowedAlgorithms.length is non-zero, so checkAreCompatibleAlgorithms runs.
All-HS shortcut returns ['HS256'] without parsing the PEM.
hsAlgorithms.includes(...) is true, so prepareKeyOrSecret makes a secret key from the PEM bytes.
Async path, by contrast, detects the key without providedAlgorithms, gets RS algorithms, and checkAreCompatibleAlgorithms throws (fail-closed).

finding.guards_checked: crypto.js:218-222 shortcut (intentional, documented in code); verifier.js:458-462 async compatibility check does not run on the sync path. Repro: createVerifier({key: publicPem, algorithms:['HS256']}) then sign HS256 with the same PEM text as the secret.

finding.claim: [low] RegExp claim matchers are unanchored, and ReDoS-prone patterns only produce a warning, so an issuer-controlled iss/aud string can match a loose pattern.
finding.source: Claim value (iss, aud, sub, jti, nonce) from a token signed by a key the verifier trusts. In multi-issuer or key-per-issuer setups, the issuer may be attacker-controlled.

trace.note: RegExp is wrapped and test() is called directly, so there is no anchoring.
checkForUnsafeRegExp only calls process.emitWarning; the pattern is still used.
validateClaimValues runs allowed.some(a => a.test(v)) on the attacker-influenced value.

finding.guards_checked: verifier.js:58-81 filtering of falsy entries (fail-closed for empty lists); type check verifier.js:183. Repro: allowedIss: /https:\/\/login\.example\.com/ accepts https://login.example.com.attacker.net.

finding.claim: [low] Signer header option is spread after alg, so an option header can override alg and produce a token whose header alg differs from the algorithm actually used to sign.
finding.source: Developer-supplied header option; exploitable only if request data reaches it.
finding.sink: Token issuance: mislabeled alg in the signed header.

trace.note: header = { alg: algorithm, typ, kid, ...additionalHeader }: additionalHeader wins.
Signature uses the real algorithm, not header.alg.

finding.guards_checked: signer.js:296-298 only checks that header is an object; no alg consistency check.

finding.claim: [low] secp256k1 keys are mapped to ES256, which is a P-256 algorithm under RFC 7518 3.4, so cross-curve keys are accepted for ES256.
finding.source: A secp256k1 public or private key configured for ES256 (operator-chosen).
finding.sink: Protected operation: ES256 signature verification or issuance.

trace.note: performDetectPublicKeyAlgorithms returns [ES256] for a secp256k1 key.
checkAreCompatibleAlgorithms passes for ES256, so the key is accepted.

finding.guards_checked: crypto.js:124-128 curve must exist in the table (secp256k1 is in it); no P-256-only check. Impact depends on whether the same key is used in other ECDSA protocols.

finding.claim: [low] The private-key algorithm cache is keyed by the key string only, so a cached result from one signer config is reused for another with the same PEM (cross-config contamination).
finding.source: Two signers in the same process using the same PEM private key string with different algorithm options.
finding.sink: Protected operation: algorithm selection at signing time.

trace.note: privateKeysCache.get(key) ignores providedAlgorithm.
An HS providedAlgorithm returns early, and the result (e.g. HS256) is cached under the key string (crypto.js:202).
A later signer with no algorithm receives HS256 and signs HMAC with the PEM text.

finding.guards_checked: signer.js:154-156 and 235-236 compatibility checks catch some mismatches (fail-closed). Mostly availability or wrong-alg issuance; no direct auth bypass found.
